prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1193; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a left-turn collision at an intersection involving a claimant who reports a concussion. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy record and confirmed the driver is named on the policy and the coverage was active at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene, and spoke with the responding officer who confirmed the claimant's presence.

Entry 4: Scene photographs were received and show some details of the impact, but no independent witnesses have come forward to describe how the collision happened.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle damage, which is consistent with the described impact pattern for a left-turn collision. Parts list and repair estimate were requested from the repair facility.

Entry 6: Took a recorded statement from the claimant regarding the crash sequence. The account covered the turn, the point of impact, and the immediate aftermath.

Entry 7: Follow-up call with the claimant's attorney. The account given through counsel matched the claimant's recorded statement in every detail discussed so far.

Entry 8: Checked prior claims and vehicle history. No earlier damage to this vehicle is on record, and no prior injury claims involving the same body area have been identified.

Entry 9: Medical records requested. Initial treatment reports describe a concussion, and the care so far appears to be a usual course for this kind of injury.

Entry 10: Reviewed the treatment timeline. Treatment has tapered off as the claimant has improved, though the file does not yet establish whether the injury came from this crash.

Entry 11: Spoke with the treating provider's office to confirm the treatment dates and the current status. Records indicate the claimant's symptoms have been easing over the recent period.

Entry 12: Reserve reviewed and file remains open pending receipt of the complete medical records and the repair estimate. Causation of the claimed injury is still under evaluation.
